source: What makes a figure a quadrilateral?
videos.handover: Next: find how the carpenter must join the two strips so the thread makes a rectangle.
videos.note: The chapter opener: what makes a four-sided figure a quadrilateral, and the carpenter's problem of joining two strips so a thread through their ends makes a rectangle. Photo ph_carpenter_frames is the backdrop of the first beat.

source: The carpenter has one strip 8 cm long. How long must the oth

items.question: The carpenter has one strip 8 cm long. How long must the other strip be for the thread to make a rectangle?
steps: Model the strips as the diagonals AC and BD of a rectangle ABCD, with AC = 8 cm.
In ∆ADC and ∆DAB: AB = CD, ∠BAD = ∠CDA = 90°, and AD is a common side.
By the SAS condition, ∆ADC ≅ ∆DAB.
So AC = BD, as corresponding parts of congruent triangles.
The other strip must be 8 cm long.
items.answer: 8 cm, because the diagonals of a rectangle are equal

videos.answer: 8 cm, because the diagonals of a rectangle are equal

source: In rectangle ABCD the diagonals meet at O and AC = 8 cm. Fin

items.question: In rectangle ABCD the diagonals meet at O and AC = 8 cm. Find OA, OC, OB and OD.
steps: In ∆AOB and ∆COD: AB = CD, ∠AOB = ∠COD (vertically opposite), and ∠ABD = ∠CDB (each is 90° minus the same angle).
By the AAS condition, ∆AOB ≅ ∆COD, so OA = OC and OB = OD.
The diagonals are equal, so BD = AC = 8 cm.
Each half is 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm.
items.answer: OA = OC = OB = OD = 4 cm; the strips are joined at their midpoints

videos.answer: OA = OC = OB = OD = 4 cm; the strips are joined at their midpoints

source: Two equal diagonals bisect each other and meet at 60°. Find

items.question: Two equal diagonals bisect each other and meet at 60°. Find all the angles of the quadrilateral ABCD and say what it is.
steps: The four angles at O are 60°, 120°, 60° and 120°.
In ∆AOB, OA = OB, so its two base angles are equal. Their sum is 180 − 60 = 120, so each is 120 ÷ 2 = 60.
In ∆AOD the angle at O is 120°, so its base angles add to 180 − 120 = 60, and each is 30.
Each corner of ABCD is made of one angle of each kind: 60 + 30 = 90.
∆AOB ≅ ∆COD and ∆AOD ≅ ∆COB by SAS, so AB = CD and AD = CB.
items.answer: Every angle of ABCD is 90° and its opposite sides are equal, so ABCD is a rectangle

videos.answer: Every angle of ABCD is 90° and its opposite sides are equal, so ABCD is a rectangle

source: Equal diagonals bisect each other at 40°. Find the angles of

items.question: Equal diagonals bisect each other at 40°. Find the angles of the quadrilateral.
steps: In the triangle with 40° at O, the base angles add to 180 − 40 = 140, so each is 140 ÷ 2 = 70.
The next triangle has 180 − 40 = 140 at O, so its base angles add to 180 − 140 = 40, and each is 20.
Each corner of the quadrilateral is 70 + 20 = 90.
items.answer: All four angles are 90°, so it is again a rectangle

videos.answer: All four angles are 90°, so it is again a rectangle

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 2)

items.question: Draw a quadrilateral whose diagonals have equal lengths of 8 cm that bisect each other, and intersect at an angle of (i) 30° (ii) 40° (iii) 90° (iv) 140°.
steps: Draw AC = 8 cm and mark its midpoint O, so OA = OC = 4 cm.
At O draw a line making the given angle with OC.
On this line mark B and D on opposite sides of O with OB = OD = 4 cm, so BD = 8 cm.
Join A, B, C and D in order.
The diagonals are equal and bisect each other, so each figure is a rectangle; at 90° all four sides are also equal.
items.answer: All four are rectangles; the one with diagonals at 90° is a square

videos.answer: All four are rectangles; the one with diagonals at 90° is a square

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 4)

items.question: We have seen how to get 90° using paper folding. Now, suppose we do not have any paper but two sticks of equal length, and a thread. How do we make an exact 90° using these?
steps: Cross the two equal sticks so that their midpoints meet at O.
Pass the thread round the four ends of the sticks in order.
The sticks are equal diagonals that bisect each other, so the thread makes a rectangle.
Every corner of a rectangle is 90°, so the thread turns through an exact 90° at each stick end.
items.answer: Cross the sticks at their midpoints and run the thread round the four ends; each corner of the thread is exactly 90°

videos.answer: Cross the sticks at their midpoints and run the thread round the four ends; each corner of the thread is exactly 90°

source: ABCD has all four angles 90°. Show that AD = CB and DC = BA,

items.question: ABCD has all four angles 90°. Show that AD = CB and DC = BA, and say why writing ∆BAD ≅ ∆CDB is wrong.
steps: Join the diagonal BD.
∠BAD = ∠DCB = 90°, and BD is common to ∆BAD and ∆DCB.
∠ABD + ∠DBC = 90° and ∠CDB + ∠DBC = 90°, so ∠ABD = ∠CDB.
By AAS, ∆BAD ≅ ∆DCB, matching B with D, A with C and D with B.
So AD = CB and BA = DC.
∆CDB would match A with D, but the right angle at A matches the right angle at C, not D.
items.answer: AD = CB and DC = BA; ∆BAD ≅ ∆CDB is wrong because the vertices are not in matching order

videos.answer: AD = CB and DC = BA; ∆BAD ≅ ∆CDB is wrong because the vertices are not in matching order

source: In rectangle ABCD, show that AB is parallel to DC.

items.question: In rectangle ABCD, show that AB is parallel to DC.
steps: Take AD as a transversal to the lines AB and DC.
The internal angles on the same side of AD are ∠A and ∠D.
Internal angles on the same side of a transversal adding to 180° means the lines are parallel.
items.answer: AB || DC

videos.answer: AB || DC

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 1)

items.question: Find all the other angles inside the following rectangles. (i) Rectangle ABCD with diagonals meeting at O and ∠CAB = 30°. (ii) Rectangle PQRS with diagonals meeting at O and ∠QOR = 110°.
steps: (i) OA = OB, because the diagonals are equal and bisect each other, so ∠ABD = ∠CAB = 30°.
∠CAD = 90 − 30 = 60, and OA = OD gives ∠ADB = 60.
In the same way ∠BDC = 30, ∠ACD = 30 and ∠ACB = 60.
(ii) ∠POS = ∠QOR = 110 (vertically opposite), and ∠QOP = ∠ROS = 180 − 110 = 70.
In isosceles ∆QOR the base angles add to 180 − 110 = 70, so ∠OQR = ∠ORQ = 35.
∠OQP = 90 − 35 = 55, and in the same way ∠OPQ = ∠ORS = ∠OSR = 55 and ∠OPS = ∠OSP = 35.
items.answer: (i) ∠ABD = 30°, ∠CAD = 60°, ∠ADB = 60°, ∠BDC = 30°, ∠ACD = 30°, ∠ACB = 60°, with 120° and 60° at O; (ii) ∠POS = 110°, ∠QOP = ∠ROS = 70°, ∠OQR = ∠ORQ = 35°, ∠OQP = ∠OPQ = ∠ORS = ∠OSR = 55°, ∠OPS = ∠OSP = 35°

videos.answer: (i) ∠ABD = 30°, ∠CAD = 60°, ∠ADB = 60°, ∠BDC = 30°, ∠ACD = 30°, ∠ACB = 60°, with 120° and 60° at O; (ii) ∠POS = 110°, ∠QOP = ∠ROS = 70°, ∠OQR = ∠ORQ = 35°, ∠OQP = ∠OPQ = ∠ORS = ∠OSR = 55°, ∠OPS = ∠OSP = 35°

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 5)

items.question: We saw that one of the properties of a rectangle is that its opposite sides are parallel. Can this be chosen as a definition of a rectangle? In other words, is every quadrilateral that has opposite sides parallel and equal, a rectangle?
steps: Draw two pairs of parallel lines that do not meet at right angles.
They make a quadrilateral with opposite sides parallel and equal, for example with angles 60°, 120°, 60° and 120°.
Its angles are not 90°, so it is not a rectangle.
items.answer: No; a slanted parallelogram has opposite sides parallel and equal but is not a rectangle

videos.answer: No; a slanted parallelogram has opposite sides parallel and equal but is not a rectangle

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 5)

items.question: If PAIR and RODS are two rectangles, find ∠IOD. (O lies on AI, ∠ORI = 30°, PR = 5 cm and RS = 5 cm.)
steps: In ∆ROI, ∠RIO = 90° because PAIR is a rectangle, and ∠ORI = 30°.
∠ROD = 90° because RODS is a rectangle.

source: Four quadrilaterals each have all angles 90°: 5 cm by 2 cm,

items.question: Four quadrilaterals each have all angles 90°: 5 cm by 2 cm, 6 cm by 3.6 cm, 5 cm by 1 cm, and 4 cm by 4 cm. Which are rectangles and which are squares?
steps: A rectangle is a quadrilateral whose angles are all 90°, so all four are rectangles.
A square also needs all four sides equal.
Only the 4 cm by 4 cm figure has equal sides.
items.answer: All four are rectangles; only the 4 cm by 4 cm one is also a square

videos.answer: All four are rectangles; only the 4 cm by 4 cm one is also a square

source: Construct a square with a diagonal of 8 cm.

items.question: Construct a square with a diagonal of 8 cm.
steps: Draw AC = 8 cm and mark its midpoint O, so OA = OC = 4 cm.
Draw the line through O perpendicular to AC.
On it mark B and D on opposite sides of O with OB = OD = 4 cm.
Join A, B, C and D in order.
The diagonals are equal, bisect each other and meet at 90°, so ABCD is a square.
items.answer: ABCD, with diagonals AC = BD = 8 cm crossing at right angles at their midpoints, is the square

videos.answer: ABCD, with diagonals AC = BD = 8 cm crossing at right angles at their midpoints, is the square

source: In square ABCD the diagonal AC is drawn. Find ∠DAC and ∠DCA.

items.question: In square ABCD the diagonal AC is drawn. Find ∠DAC and ∠DCA.
steps: In ∆ADC the angle at D is a right angle, so ∠DAC and ∠DCA share 180 − 90 = 90.
AD = DC, so the angles opposite them are equal: ∠DAC = ∠DCA.
So each is 90 ÷ 2 = 45.
items.answer: ∠DAC = ∠DCA = 45°, so the diagonal bisects the right angles

videos.answer: ∠DAC = ∠DCA = 45°, so the diagonal bisects the right angles

source: Figure it Out (rectangles and squares, question 3)

items.question: Consider a circle with centre O. Line segments PL and AM are two perpendicular diameters of the circle. What is the figure APML? Reason and/or experiment to figure this out.
steps: AM and PL are the diagonals of APML.
Both are diameters, so they are equal.
Both pass through the centre O and OA = OM = OP = OL (radii), so they bisect each other.
They are perpendicular, so they meet at 90°.
Equal diagonals that bisect each other at 90° make a square.
items.answer: APML is a square

videos.answer: APML is a square

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 6)

items.question: Construct a square with diagonal 6 cm without using a protractor.
steps: Draw AB = 6 cm.
With the compass open more than 3 cm, draw arcs from A and from B on both sides of AB; join the two crossing points. This line is perpendicular to AB through its midpoint O.
With the compass set to 3 cm and centre O, mark C and D on this line on opposite sides of AB.
Join A, C, B and D in order.
The diagonals are 6 cm each, bisect each other and meet at 90°, so ACBD is a square.
items.answer: ACBD is the square, with diagonals AB = CD = 6 cm

videos.answer: ACBD is the square, with diagonals AB = CD = 6 cm

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 7)

items.question: CASE is a square. The points U, V, W and X are the midpoints of the sides of the square. What type of quadrilateral is UVWX? Find this by using geometric reasoning, as well as by construction and measurement. Find other ways of constructing a square within a square such that the vertices of the inner square lie on the sides of the outer square.
steps: At each corner of CASE the two half sides are equal and the corner angle is 90°.
So the four corner triangles are congruent by SAS, and UV = VW = WX = XU.
Each corner triangle is isosceles and right-angled, so its base angles are 45° each.
On a side, the two 45° angles and the angle of UVWX make a straight angle: 180 − 45 − 45 = 90.
UVWX has four equal sides and four right angles, so it is a square.
Marking four points the same distance from each corner, all going the same way round, again gives four congruent right triangles and so another square.
items.answer: UVWX is a square; any four points at the same distance from the corners, taken the same way round, also make a square

videos.answer: UVWX is a square; any four points at the same distance from the corners, taken the same way round, also make a square

source: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 75°, 95° and 110°. Find

items.question: Three angles of a quadrilateral are 75°, 95° and 110°. Find the fourth angle.
steps: A diagonal splits the quadrilateral into two triangles, so its angles add up to 180 + 180 = 360.
The three known angles add up to 75 + 95 + 110 = 280.
The fourth angle is 360 − 280 = 80.

source: A quadrilateral has three angles of 90°. Find the fourth ang

items.question: A quadrilateral has three angles of 90°. Find the fourth angle.
steps: The angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360.
The three right angles add up to 90 + 90 + 90 = 270.
The fourth angle is 360 − 270 = 90.
items.answer: 90°, so the quadrilateral is a rectangle

videos.answer: 90°, so the quadrilateral is a rectangle

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 10)

items.question: Will the sum of the angles in a quadrilateral such as the following one also be 360°? Find the answer using geometric reasoning as well as by constructing this figure and measuring. (ABCD has one corner that caves in.)
steps: Draw the diagonal from the caved-in corner to the opposite corner; it lies inside the figure.
It splits ABCD into two triangles, each with angles adding up to 180.
At the caved-in corner the two triangle angles together make the reflex angle of ABCD.
So the four angles of ABCD add up to 180 + 180 = 360.
items.answer: Yes; the angle sum is still 360°, using the diagonal that lies inside the figure

videos.answer: Yes; the angle sum is still 360°, using the diagonal that lies inside the figure

source: Construct a parallelogram ABCD with AB = 4 cm, AD = 5 cm and

items.question: Construct a parallelogram ABCD with AB = 4 cm, AD = 5 cm and an angle of 30° between them.
steps: Draw AB = 4 cm.
At A draw a 30° angle and mark D on its arm with AD = 5 cm.
Through D draw a line parallel to AB; through B draw a line parallel to AD.
Mark the point where these two lines meet as C.
ABCD has both pairs of opposite sides parallel, so it is a parallelogram.
items.answer: ABCD is the required parallelogram, and it is not a rectangle

videos.answer: ABCD is the required parallelogram, and it is not a rectangle

source: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 30°. Find ∠B, ∠C and ∠D.

items.question: In parallelogram ABCD, ∠A = 30°. Find ∠B, ∠C and ∠D.
steps: AB || CD with transversal AD, so ∠A + ∠D = 180.
AD || BC with transversal AB, so ∠A + ∠B = 180, and ∠B = 150.

source: In parallelogram ABCD, AB = 4 cm and AD = 5 cm. Find CB and

items.question: In parallelogram ABCD, AB = 4 cm and AD = 5 cm. Find CB and CD, and say why ∆ABD ≅ ∆CBD is wrong.
steps: Join the diagonal BD.
∠BAD = ∠DCB, because they are opposite angles of the parallelogram.
AD || BC with transversal BD, so ∠ADB = ∠CBD (alternate angles).
BD is common, so by AAS ∆ABD ≅ ∆CDB.
So CB = AD = 5 cm and CD = AB = 4 cm.
∆CBD would match A with C but B with B, claiming AB equals CB, yet AB is 4 cm and CB is 5 cm.
items.answer: CB = 5 cm and CD = 4 cm; ∆ABD ≅ ∆CBD is wrong because its vertices do not match

videos.answer: CB = 5 cm and CD = 4 cm; ∆ABD ≅ ∆CBD is wrong because its vertices do not match

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 9)

items.question: What type of a quadrilateral is one in which the opposite sides are equal? Justify your answer. (Hint: Draw a diagonal and check for congruent triangles.)
steps: Let ABCD have AB = CD and AD = CB, and draw the diagonal BD.
∆ABD ≅ ∆CDB by SSS, because BD is common.
So ∠ABD = ∠CDB; these are alternate angles for AB and DC with transversal BD, so AB || DC.
Also ∠ADB = ∠CBD, so AD || BC.
Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
items.answer: A parallelogram

videos.answer: A parallelogram

source: In parallelogram EASY the diagonals AY and ES meet at O, wit

items.question: In parallelogram EASY the diagonals AY and ES meet at O, with AY = 10 cm and ES = 6 cm. Find OA, OY, OE and OS, and say why ∆AOE ≅ ∆SOY is wrong.
steps: AE = YS, because they are opposite sides of the parallelogram.
AE || YS, so ∠OAE = ∠OYS and ∠OEA = ∠OSY (alternate angles).
By ASA, ∆AOE ≅ ∆YOS, so OA = OY and OE = OS.
OA = OY = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm and OE = OS = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm.
∆SOY would pair A with S and E with Y, but A matches Y and E matches S.
items.answer: OA = OY = 5 cm and OE = OS = 3 cm; ∆SOY is in the wrong order

videos.answer: OA = OY = 5 cm and OE = OS = 3 cm; ∆SOY is in the wrong order

source: Figure it Out (parallelograms and rhombuses, question 2)

items.question: Using the diagonal properties, construct a parallelogram whose diagonals are of lengths 7 cm and 5 cm, and intersect at an angle of 140°.
steps: Draw AC = 7 cm and mark its midpoint O, so OA = OC = 3.5 cm.
At O draw a line making 140° with OC.
On it mark B and D on opposite sides of O with OB = OD = 2.5 cm, so BD = 5 cm.
Join A, B, C and D in order.
The diagonals bisect each other, so ABCD is a parallelogram.
items.answer: ABCD, with diagonals 7 cm and 5 cm bisecting each other at 140°, is the parallelogram

videos.answer: ABCD, with diagonals 7 cm and 5 cm bisecting each other at 140°, is the parallelogram

source: Construct a quadrilateral ABCD with all sides 5 cm and ∠A =

items.question: Construct a quadrilateral ABCD with all sides 5 cm and ∠A = 50°.
steps: Draw AB = 5 cm.
At A draw a 50° angle and mark D on its arm with AD = 5 cm.
With the compass set to 5 cm, draw an arc from B and an arc from D.
Mark the point where the arcs cross as C, and join BC and DC.
AB = BC = CD = DA = 5 cm, so ABCD is a rhombus.
items.answer: ABCD is a rhombus with a 50° angle, and it is not a square

videos.answer: ABCD is a rhombus with a 50° angle, and it is not a square

source: Rhombus ABCD has ∠A = 50°. Find its other angles.

items.question: Rhombus ABCD has ∠A = 50°. Find its other angles.
steps: Diagonal BD makes four equal angles a: two at B and two at D.
In ∆ADB, a + a + 50 = 180, so the two angles a add up to 180 − 50 = 130.
Each is 130 ÷ 2 = 65.
∠B = ∠D = 65 + 65 = 130, and ∠C = ∠A = 50, because a rhombus is a parallelogram.
items.answer: The angles are 50°, 130°, 50° and 130°

videos.answer: The angles are 50°, 130°, 50° and 130°

source: In rhombus GAME the diagonals meet at O, with GM = 8 cm and

items.question: In rhombus GAME the diagonals meet at O, with GM = 8 cm and EA = 6 cm. Find the angle at O, GO and EO.
steps: A rhombus is a parallelogram, so its diagonals bisect each other: GO = MO and EO = AO.
In ∆GEO and ∆MEO: GE = ME, GO = MO, and EO is common, so ∆GEO ≅ ∆MEO by SSS.
So ∠GOE = ∠MOE, and together they make 180, so each is 90.
GO = 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm and EO = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm.
items.answer: The diagonals meet at 90°; GO = 4 cm and EO = 3 cm

videos.answer: The diagonals meet at 90°; GO = 4 cm and EO = 3 cm

source: Figure it Out (parallelograms and rhombuses, question 1)

items.question: Find the remaining angles in the following quadrilaterals. (i) Parallelogram PEAR with ∠P = 40°. (ii) Parallelogram PQRS with ∠P = 110°. (iii) Rhombus UVWX with diagonal XV and ∠XVU = 30°. (iv) Rhombus OIEA with diagonal OE and ∠OEA = 20°.
steps: (i) Adjacent angles add up to 180, so ∠E = ∠R = 180 − 40 = 140, and ∠A = ∠P = 40.
(iii) The diagonal XV bisects ∠V and ∠X, so ∠V = 30 + 30 = 60 and ∠X = 60.
(iv) The diagonal OE bisects ∠E and ∠O, so ∠E = 20 + 20 = 40 and ∠O = 40.

source: Figure it Out (parallelograms and rhombuses, question 3)

items.question: Using the diagonal properties, construct a rhombus whose diagonals are of lengths 4 cm and 5 cm.
steps: Draw AC = 5 cm and mark its midpoint O.
Draw the line through O perpendicular to AC.
On it mark B and D on opposite sides of O with OB = OD = 2 cm, so BD = 4 cm.
Join A, B, C and D in order.
The diagonals bisect each other at 90°, so all four sides are equal and ABCD is a rhombus.
items.answer: ABCD, with diagonals 5 cm and 4 cm bisecting each other at right angles, is the rhombus

videos.answer: ABCD, with diagonals 5 cm and 4 cm bisecting each other at right angles, is the rhombus

source: Two rubber bands of 4 cm cross at right angles at their midp

items.question: Two rubber bands of 4 cm cross at right angles at their midpoints. Name the quadrilateral their ends make, and name it again after one band is extended by 2 cm at each end.
steps: The diagonals are equal and bisect each other, so the quadrilateral is a rectangle.
They also meet at 90°, so all four sides are equal: it is a square.
The extended band is now 2 + 4 + 2 = 8 cm long and still has its midpoint at the crossing.
The diagonals still bisect each other at 90°, so all four sides are equal, but the diagonals are 4 cm and 8 cm, so it is not a rectangle.
items.answer: First a square; after extending one diagonal, a rhombus

videos.answer: First a square; after extending one diagonal, a rhombus

source: Join two copies of the triangle with sides 8 cm, 8 cm and 6

items.question: Join two copies of the triangle with sides 8 cm, 8 cm and 6 cm in different ways and name the quadrilaterals.
steps: Along the 6 cm side: the four outer sides are all 8 cm, so the quadrilateral is a rhombus.
Along an 8 cm side, with one copy turned half round: the outer sides are 8, 6, 8 and 6 cm, opposite sides are equal, so it is a parallelogram.
Along an 8 cm side, with one copy flipped over: two neighbouring sides are 8 cm and the other two are 6 cm, so it is a kite.
Two equilateral triangles of 8 cm, joined in the same way, give four sides of 8 cm: a rhombus.
items.answer: A rhombus, a parallelogram and a kite; two equilateral triangles give a rhombus

videos.answer: A rhombus, a parallelogram and a kite; two equilateral triangles give a rhombus

source: Two copies of a triangle with sides 6 cm, 9 cm and 12 cm are

items.question: Two copies of a triangle with sides 6 cm, 9 cm and 12 cm are joined along a side. List the quadrilaterals you can get.
steps: Along the 6 cm side, turned half round: sides 9, 12, 9 and 12, a parallelogram.
Along the 9 cm side, turned half round: sides 6, 12, 6 and 12, a parallelogram.
Along the 12 cm side, turned half round: sides 6, 9, 6 and 9, a parallelogram.
Flipped over the 12 cm side: sides 6, 6, 9 and 9 with equal neighbours, a kite.
Flipped over the 6 cm or the 9 cm side: again two pairs of equal neighbouring sides, a kite, but one that caves in at a corner.
items.answer: Three parallelograms and three kites; only the kite on the 12 cm side has no corner that caves in

videos.answer: Three parallelograms and three kites; only the kite on the 12 cm side has no corner that caves in

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 1)

items.question: Find all the sides and the angles of the quadrilateral obtained by joining two equilateral triangles with sides 4 cm.
steps: Each side of the quadrilateral is a side of an equilateral triangle, so all four sides are 4 cm.
Each angle of an equilateral triangle is 60.
The two corners not on the joined side are single triangle angles: 60 each.
The two corners on the joined side are made of two triangle angles: 60 + 60 = 120 each.
items.answer: All sides are 4 cm; the angles are 60°, 120°, 60° and 120°, a rhombus

videos.answer: All sides are 4 cm; the angles are 60°, 120°, 60° and 120°, a rhombus

source: ABCD is a kite with AB = BC and CD = DA, and its diagonals m

items.question: ABCD is a kite with AB = BC and CD = DA, and its diagonals meet at O. Show that BD bisects ∠ABC and that BD is perpendicular to AC with AO = OC.
steps: In ∆ABD and ∆CBD: AB = CB, AD = CD, and BD is common, so ∆ABD ≅ ∆CBD by SSS.
So ∠ABD = ∠CBD: BD bisects ∠ABC (and likewise ∠ADC).
In ∆AOB and ∆COB: AB = CB, ∠ABO = ∠CBO, and BO is common, so ∆AOB ≅ ∆COB by SAS.
So AO = OC, and ∠AOB = ∠COB.
These two angles make a straight angle of 180, so each is 180 ÷ 2 = 90.
items.answer: BD bisects ∠ABC and ∠ADC, and it cuts AC in half at right angles

videos.answer: BD bisects ∠ABC and ∠ADC, and it cuts AC in half at right angles

source: Figure it Out (kites and trapeziums, question 2)

items.question: Construct a kite whose diagonals are of lengths 6 cm and 8 cm.
steps: Draw AC = 6 cm and draw its perpendicular bisector, meeting AC at O.
On the bisector mark B 2 cm from O on one side and D 6 cm from O on the other side, so BD = 2 + 6 = 8 cm.
Join A, B, C and D in order.
B and D lie on the perpendicular bisector of AC, so BA = BC and DA = DC: ABCD is a kite.
Splitting 8 cm as 4 cm and 4 cm would give a rhombus, which is a special kite.
items.answer: ABCD with AC = 6 cm, BD = 8 cm, BD the perpendicular bisector of AC and O not the midpoint of BD

videos.answer: ABCD with AC = 6 cm, BD = 8 cm, BD the perpendicular bisector of AC and O not the midpoint of BD

source: Trapezium PQRS has PQ || SR, ∠P = 70° and ∠Q = 55°. Find ∠S

items.question: Trapezium PQRS has PQ || SR, ∠P = 70° and ∠Q = 55°. Find ∠S and ∠R.
steps: PS is a transversal to the parallel lines PQ and SR, so ∠S + ∠P = 180.
QR is a transversal too, so ∠R = 180 − 55 = 125.

source: UVWX is an isosceles trapezium with UV || XW, UX = VW and ∠U

items.question: UVWX is an isosceles trapezium with UV || XW, UX = VW and ∠U = 65°. Find ∠V, ∠W and ∠X.
steps: Draw XY and WZ perpendicular to UV; XWZY is a rectangle, so XY = WZ.
∆UXY and ∆VWZ have right angles at Y and Z, UX = VW and XY = WZ, so ∆UXY ≅ ∆VWZ by RHS.
UX is a transversal to the parallel sides, so ∠X = 180 − 65 = 115, and likewise ∠W = 115.

items.question: Find the remaining angles in the following trapeziums. (i) A trapezium with angles 105° and 135° at the ends of one parallel side. (ii) An isosceles trapezium with an angle of 100°.
steps: (i) Each slanting side is a transversal to the parallel sides, so its two angles add up to 180.
The remaining angles are 180 − 105 = 75 and 180 − 135 = 45.
(ii) The slanting sides are equal, so the angles at the ends of the same parallel side are equal: the other one next to 100 is also 100.
The angles below them are 180 − 100 = 80 each.

source: Give every family name that belongs to a square.

items.question: Give every family name that belongs to a square.
steps: All its angles are 90°, so it is a rectangle.
All its sides are equal, so it is a rhombus.
Its opposite sides are parallel, so it is a parallelogram, and so also a trapezium.
Its neighbouring sides are equal in two pairs, so it is a kite.
items.answer: A square is a rectangle, a rhombus, a parallelogram, a trapezium and a kite

items.question: The diagonals AC and BD of ABCD bisect each other at O at right angles. Show that ABCD is a rhombus.
steps: OA = OC and OB = OD, because the diagonals bisect each other.
The four angles at O are each 90.
In ∆AOB and ∆COB: OA = OC, ∠AOB = ∠COB, and OB is common, so they are congruent by SAS and AB = CB.
In the same way BC = CD and CD = DA.
All four sides are equal, so ABCD is a rhombus.
items.answer: ABCD is a rhombus

items.question: Draw a Venn diagram showing the set of parallelograms, kites, rhombuses, rectangles, and squares. Then, answer the following questions. (i) What is the quadrilateral that is both a kite and a parallelogram? (ii) Can there be a quadrilateral that is both a kite and a rectangle? (iii) Is every kite a rhombus? If not, what is the correct relationship between these two types of quadrilaterals?
steps: Draw parallelograms holding rectangles and rhombuses, with squares in their overlap; draw kites overlapping parallelograms exactly in the rhombuses.
(i) A parallelogram has opposite sides equal; a kite has neighbouring sides equal in pairs, so all four sides are equal: a rhombus (squares included).
(ii) A kite that is a rectangle has equal neighbouring sides and opposite sides equal, so all sides are equal and all angles 90°: a square.
(iii) No. A kite can have sides 6, 6, 9 and 9, which is not a rhombus. Every rhombus is a kite.
items.answer: (i) A rhombus; (ii) Yes, a square; (iii) No; every rhombus is a kite, but not every kite is a rhombus

videos.answer: (i) A rhombus; (ii) Yes, a square; (iii) No; every rhombus is a kite, but not every kite is a rhombus

items.question: If a quadrilateral has four equal sides and one angle of 90°, will it be a square? Find the answer using geometric reasoning as well as by construction and measurement.
steps: Four equal sides make it a rhombus, so it is a parallelogram.
Adjacent angles of a parallelogram add up to 180, so the neighbours of 90 are 180 − 90 = 90.
The opposite angle equals 90 too, so all four angles are 90.
Four equal sides and four right angles make a square.
items.answer: Yes, it is a square

videos.answer: Yes, it is a square

items.question: State whether the following statements are true or false. Justify your answers. (i) A quadrilateral whose diagonals are equal and bisect each other must be a square. (ii) A quadrilateral having three right angles must be a rectangle. (iii) A quadrilateral whose diagonals bisect each other must be a parallelogram. (iv) A quadrilateral whose diagonals are perpendicular to each other must be a rhombus. (v) A quadrilateral in which the opposite angles are equal must be a parallelogram. (vi) A quadrilateral in which all the angles are equal is a rectangle. (vii) Isosceles trapeziums are parallelograms.
steps: (i) False: such diagonals give a rectangle, which need not be a square.
(ii) True: the fourth angle is 360 − 270 = 90.
(iii) True: the triangles at the crossing are congruent in opposite pairs, giving equal alternate angles, so opposite sides are parallel.
(iv) False: a kite has perpendicular diagonals but need not be a rhombus.
(v) True: with angles x, y, x, y we get 2x + 2y = 360, so neighbouring angles add up to 180 and opposite sides are parallel.
(vi) True: each angle is 360 ÷ 4 = 90.
(vii) False: its slanting sides are not parallel, unless it is a rectangle.
items.answer: (i) False (ii) True (iii) True (iv) False (v) True (vi) True (vii) False

videos.answer: (i) False (ii) True (iii) True (iv) False (v) True (vi) True (vii) False

items.question: A sheet is folded in half and then into a quarter, and one slanting crease is made across the corner at the middle of the sheet. What shape do the creases make, and how should you fold to get a square?
steps: The two folds cross at right angles at the centre of the sheet.
Unfolding copies the crease into all four quarters, so the shape has four equal sides.
Its diagonals lie along the folds, so they bisect each other at right angles: a rhombus.
Several creases parallel to the first give rhombuses inside one another.
If the crease cuts off equal lengths along both folds, the diagonals are equal too, and the rhombus is a square.
items.answer: A rhombus; fold the crease at 45°, cutting equal lengths on both folds, to get a square

videos.answer: A rhombus; fold the crease at 45°, cutting equal lengths on both folds, to get a square
